Learn MACs dynamically and keep them

head: Item
Detail
rows: Blocking, Listening, Learning, Forwarding, Disabled (about 30 to 50 s to converge)
Root (best path to root), Designated (forwards on a segment), Alternate / Backup (RSTP), Non-designated (STP)
Lowest bridge ID: priority (default 32768 + VLAN ID, steps of 4096) then lowest MAC
PVST+ (STP per VLAN), Rapid PVST+ (`spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst`), MST

blocks.title: EtherChannel and first-hop redundancy
items: EtherChannel needs matching speed, duplex, VLAN/trunk settings on every member. LACP active/passive (open standard), PAgP desirable/auto (Cisco), `on` (static, no negotiation). Two passive or two auto sides do not form a bundle.
HSRP (Cisco): active and standby routers share a virtual IP; default priority 100, preempt off by default. VRRP is the open standard; GLBP load-balances (Cisco).

blocks.title: OSPF
rows: Set the router ID (else highest loopback, then highest active interface IP)
Advertise the network but form no neighbors

blocks.title: OSPF facts
items: Neighbor states: Down, Init, 2-Way, ExStart, Exchange, Loading, Full. DR/BDR are elected on multi-access (Ethernet) segments; neighbors that are not DR/BDR stay at 2-Way.
Hello 10 s / dead 40 s on broadcast links. Hello timers, area ID, subnet, authentication and stub flags must match to form an adjacency.
Cost = reference bandwidth / interface bandwidth (default reference 100 Mbps, so FastEthernet and faster all cost 1).
Area 0 is the backbone; all areas connect to it. LSA types: 1 router, 2 network, 3 summary, 5 external.

sheets.title: IP services and security
sheets.blurb: ACLs, NAT, DHCP, NTP, syslog, SNMP, snooping.

blocks.title: ACLs, NAT and security
rows: ip access-list extended WEB  /  permit tcp any host 10.0.0.5 eq 443
interface g0/1  /  ip access-group WEB in
ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/1 overload
PAT using the outside interface address
ip nat inside  /  ip nat outside
ip dhcp snooping  /  ip dhcp snooping vlan 10  /  ip dhcp snooping trust
Trust only the uplink to the real DHCP server
Dynamic ARP inspection (uses the snooping table)

blocks.title: ACL rules of thumb
items: Top-down, first match wins, implicit `deny any` at the end. Place standard ACLs close to the destination and extended ACLs close to the source.
Inbound ACLs filter before routing; outbound after. One ACL per interface, per protocol, per direction. ACLs do not filter traffic the router itself originates.
Wildcard mask: 0 = must match, 1 = ignore. `host x` = 0.0.0.0, `any` = 255.255.255.255.

blocks.title: DHCP server, NTP, syslog, SNMP
rows: ip dhcp pool LAN  /  network 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0  /  default-router 192.168.1.1  /  dns-server 8.8.8.8
SNMPv2c read-only (v3 adds auth and encryption)

blocks.title: Security fundamentals
items: Threats: malware, phishing, social engineering, DoS/DDoS, spoofing, reconnaissance, man-in-the-middle. Mitigation = defense in depth, patching, strong passwords, MFA, user training.
AAA: authentication, authorization, accounting (RADIUS or TACACS+). Passwords: use `enable secret` (type 8/9 hashes if available) not `enable password`.
Layer 2: port security, DHCP snooping, DAI, disable unused ports, native VLAN not 1, no DTP (`switchport nonegotiate`). VPN: site-to-site and remote access (IPsec, SSL).
WPA3 beats WPA2; avoid WEP. 802.1X = port-based network access control.

sheets.title: IP addressing
sheets.blurb: Subnet table, special ranges and IPv6 address types.

blocks.title: Subnetting in four steps
items: Block size = 256 minus the interesting octet of the mask (for example /26: 256 - 192 = 64).
Network = the multiple of the block size at or below the host's value in that octet.
Broadcast = next network address minus 1; usable range sits between network and broadcast.
Hosts = 2^(host bits) - 2. Subnets = 2^(borrowed bits). Need N hosts: smallest 2^h with 2^h - 2 >= N.

blocks.title: Special IPv4 ranges
head: Range

blocks.title: IPv6 address types
head: Type
Prefix
Notes
rows: Every interface; not routed; used by NDP and routing protocols
ff02::1 all nodes, ff02::2 all routers; no broadcast in IPv6

blocks.text: IPv6 is 128 bits written as 8 groups of 4 hex digits. Drop leading zeros in a group, and replace one run of all-zero groups with `::` (once only). Standard subnet is /64. SLAAC builds an address from the router's prefix plus an interface ID (EUI-64 or random); DHCPv6 can be stateful or stateless. NDP replaces ARP.

blocks.title: Automation and programmability
items: REST uses HTTP verbs: GET read, POST create, PUT replace, PATCH modify, DELETE remove. Data formats: JSON (key: value, braces and brackets), XML, YAML.
Controller-based networking separates the control plane (decisions) from the data plane (forwarding); northbound APIs go to apps, southbound APIs (NETCONF, RESTCONF, OpenFlow) go to devices.
Cisco Catalyst Center (DNA Center) = intent-based campus management. SD-Access = fabric, SD-WAN = overlay across WAN links.
Configuration management: Ansible (agentless, YAML playbooks, push), Puppet and Chef (agent, pull), Terraform (infrastructure provisioning).
